summary: Coos County lookout on Elk's Peak: 1916 and 1925 notices name a station there, the register dates a tower to about 1941, and it is now gone.

facts.status_note: Abandoned and gone per the register and firelookout.com; no source dates its removal

events.note: A May 1916 notice plans a telephone line to the Elk's Peak lookout station; an August 1916 notice says a lookout point is to be established there
April 1925 Siuslaw News lists Elk's peak among lookout points for the year; December 1925 Coos Bay Times lists Elks Peak among Coos FPA lookout stations
Register says built about 1941; firelookout.com gives 1941 for the tower. Neither says whether it replaced the earlier station

evidence.supports: Elk Peak is in Coos County, Oregon
about 18 miles northeast of North Bend
May 1916 notice: about 17 miles of new telephone line
evidence.quote: About 17 miles of new telephone line is to be constructed this summer

evidence.supports: May 1916 telephone line to connect the Elk's Peak lookout station
evidence.quote: to connect the Elk's Peak lookout station with the Gardiner headquarters

evidence.supports: August 1916 notice about a trail: a lookout point is to be established at the peak
evidence.quote: where a lookout point is to be established

evidence.supports: April 1925 Siuslaw News: lookouts to be placed on Elk's peak this year
evidence.quote: Among the points at which lookouts will be placed this year are Dean's mountain and Elk's peak.

evidence.supports: December 1925 Coos Bay Times: Elks Peak among the lookouts Coos FPA maintained
evidence.quote: The lookout stations maintained by Coos FPA are as follows: Elks Peak, north of Allegany.

evidence.supports: register dates the tower to about 1941, later abandoned and now gone
evidence.quote: Built about 1941, this tower was later abandoned and is now gone.

evidence.supports: firelookout.com dates the tower to 1941 and lists it as abandoned and gone
Rex's page marks the site as removed, with no date
Coos FPA is the administering agency

notes_for_editor: Register and firelookout.com both date the tower to about 1941, but Rex's page quotes 1916 and 1925 newspapers that name an Elk's Peak station. A station probably predates the 1941 tower, but no source says so directly. The two 1916 notices disagree on whether a station already stood. Access is unknown and no site description was found. A Coos FPA website appeared in search results but was not read, so it is not cited. Verified 2026-10-09: the full register text and firelookout.com text were read and neither mentions a replacement.
